request: Hey Claude, I just added the "market-sizing" skill. Size our market for 2026 as TAM, SAM and SOM. We sell booking software to salons, clinics and fitness studios with 1 to 20 staff in the US, UK and Canada. Use our Search Console, Google Ads and GA4, and the search volumes. Billing numbers are below.
business: Example Booking Software, an online booking and scheduling app for small service businesses (invented example)

scope_grid_agreed.rows: vertical x country x size band; a row counts toward SAM only when its vertical, country and size band are all in SAM

verticals.tam_only: other appointment-based service businesses (spas, pet grooming, tutoring and others)
verticals.why_tam_only: no industry setup for them in the product yet

scope_grid_agreed.billing: all plans bill in USD in every country, so no currency conversion is needed

sources.what: US establishments by industry and staff size
UK businesses by industry and staff size
Canadian businesses by industry, province and staff size
share of small service businesses paying for booking software, and the share that shopped for one in the year
small business appointment scheduling software spend in the US, UK and Canada, its yearly growth to 2029, and the share by vertical
Australian businesses by industry and staff size
Irish enterprises by industry and staff size
New Zealand enterprises by industry and staff size

plan_mix_of_current_customers.label: given
plan_mix_of_current_customers.note: from billing, customers on each plan at 2026-09-30

published_figure_usd.scope: small business appointment scheduling software spend, US, UK and Canada

growth_per_year.note: the report's yearly growth for 2024 to 2029

share_from_1_to_20_staff.label: assumed
share_from_1_to_20_staff.reason: businesses with 1 to 20 staff are about 85% of buyers in the registers but buy smaller plans, so a lower share of spend

share_shopping_per_year.note: share of small service businesses that looked for booking software in 2025

searches_per_buying_journey.label: assumed
searches_per_buying_journey.reason: a buyer compares several phrases over a few sessions; no first-party measure exists

note: Example data: an invented online booking software company with invented accounts, not a real business. Every number in expected_output.json follows from this input. The published sources are invented too and use .example addresses; every count, share and growth rate attributed to them is made up for this example.
